title: Does subagent level orchestration really save context overall?
author: KidLink4
selftext:
Many harnesses are now using orchestration/review loops to execute tasks. This often includes a planning phase where the user and the LLM will back and forth about design choices, then write a spec sheet. 

What I'm wondering is, when the orchestration phase kicks in, I'm weighing continuing the same session as the orchestration device, or spawning a subagent to orchestrate directly via subsequent subagent calls, then reporting the full task back to the initial agent. 

How would this affect performance versus cost? If one is better performance wise, is the cost difference worth the performance boost?

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
It uses significantly less. The reason is because the main thread sends out the needed context to the subagent, and only what's needed. On its own, this actually doesn't save too much because cached context is significantly cheaper than fresh context to prompt. HOWEVER, when performing a large, multistep implementation, data accumulates. When it's handled via subagents, they only send back the required data and results to your main thread, so you're able to continue on that main thread without context ballooning to extremes as it keeps track of and manages your subagents. If it was the main thread doing it, by the time you finished a large implementation you'd be pushing 70-80% of a 1mil context window. The amount of tokens you're consuming per prompt at that point is huge.

For small implementations that are resolved in a single step, you should just use the main thread. The context savings are not worth the initialization and context delivery to the subagent. The better harnesses (Codex/CC) already structure their subagent dispatching this way, but you may need to outline your own custom instructions if it doesn't.

comments.author: Masterbossing
comments.body: Uhmm i believe subagents just kinda move the problems around. I literally just ended up keeping the entity state in a graph store. Was looking at HydraDB and plain postgres too, since the summaries kept drifting on me 🫥

comments.author: orblabs
comments.body: If done well, yes, it improves costs and quality exponentially. And you don't even need special harnesses, you can achieve very advanced setups with just skills nowadays. But, as with everything, there are good and bad ways of doing it, and some stuff is tied to specific models and harness with different ways of handling the setup.

replies.author: Lavio00
replies.body: I really dont understand how to go about doing this. Any tips?

replies.author: orblabs
replies.body:
Sure.   
First step, a plan. You get the best model you have access to, and you ask it to create for you a very detailed plan for what you want to achieve. You ask it to have it broke down into steps and phases (each phase made of multiple steps), each step well described and each phase with specific goals it needs to achieve and why it exists. YOu also ask to add the general reasoning behind the whole plan. You tell the smart model that the plan is for a lesser model to implement and you ask for all the big decisions to be already taken and anticipated and that everything must have a justification and rationale behind it. The plan needs to be saved into a .md file. 

You then get another model, it really depends on what you have access to. Personally, i use fable for the plans and either Opus or Sol as plan implementers.   
With opus i use this skill : [https://github.com/frozenpepper/deepseek-and-destroy](https://github.com/frozenpepper/deepseek-and-destroy)  which basically tells opus to take a plan and have an army of extremely cheap deep seek workers implement it (needs opencode go subscription and opencode cli installed on your machine). With Sol i use this other skill instead [https://github.com/frozenpepper/Lunacy](https://github.com/frozenpepper/Lunacy) which does the same but abusing Luna.   
Both skills will minimize the expensive model use (opus or sol) and abuse the cheap models for implementation, each skill studied specifically to use as little as possible of OPus or Luna usage. 

Let me know if you need more info , best luck !

replies.author: Lavio00
replies.body: Thanks a lot for this! I have openrouter but not opencode unfortunately. But that's in a totally separate workflow (VS code, I only use the opencode API to dabble in open weights models. Use it very rarely). Other than that I just use the claude app, with fable 5 as the main coding bot (Ive got max 20x plan). Is there an apt skill to use with this setup? Perhaps having fable 5 as orchestrator and opus as the skill-user?

replies.author: orblabs
replies.body:
The opencode thing is to save a ton of money. You can totally use the deepseek and destroy skill in a new Claude app session, have opus 5 to be used as orchestrator and just telling it to use Sonnet agents in the worker role. Opus should be able to autoconfigure everything. I wouldn't use fable as orchestrator as it isn't needed, it is very good at defining plans and analyzing complex situations, but i then suggest to use the results of fable work to have cheaper model operate.  
Opus + sonnet are a very powerful combo, just not very cheap.

replies.author: Lavio00
replies.body:
Oh so you're saying to show claude that link of the deepseek-and-destroy, but tell it that Opus 5 is the orchestrator and sonnet takes the role of what deepseek does in that link of yours? So it would look something like this:

Fable 5 - only use for initial planning  
Opus 5 - The Orchestrator, ie the model I actively chat with  
Sonnet 5 - the stand-in for deepseek in that deepseek-and-destroy skill

If above is correct, you're telling me to show that link to claude and just tell it to autoconfigure everything so it matches my intended workflow?

replies.author: orblabs
replies.body:
Yes, you got it. Ask claude to isntall the skill from the link, you will have to restart the Claude app then. Then, once you have a nice plan in a .md file, you start a fresh chat with opus 5 and in the first message you write something along the lines of "/deepseek-and-destroy" (this, using the '/' tells claude to load the right skill) " /deepseek-and-destroy we are going to work on the plan [xxxx.md](http://xxxx.md) but instead of the default opencode and deepseek based workers configuration you need to user sonnet 5 with medium reasoning as implementation agents"

Add custom instructions if you have specific per project guideliners, reference to special documents with guidelines etc.  
IMPORTANT : That skill is designed to implement complex plans exploiting  the fact that deepseek (and luna) are extremely cheap, it will get your work done very well with sonnet and more importantly it will stick even to very long plans (which you can also interrupt and resume etc) , BUT it probably won't be cheap. It will do a much better job than just asking opus to implement the plan (it would miss a lot of stuff if the plan is long or complex), but it will also burn a lot of tokens.  If you are on a budget, i highly suggest the 5$ opencode subscription, it gives you billions of deepseek tokens.

replies.author: Lavio00
replies.body: Thanks dude. Yeah I concur, the description I gave with opus and sonnet is good but way more expensive than your setup. Ive spent some time researching this in the meantime Ive spoken to you. Seems like ditching a claude subscription outright and just using an Anthropic API for orchestration and planing + opencode API for cheap subagents for coding is the way to go... Let me know if you disagree (ie if Ive misunderstood something).

replies.author: orblabs
replies.body:
Personally, i think that the $20 subscription is of great value. Opus is a fantastic orchestrator (at least for my needs), doing some napkin math, i think the 20$ plan would have opus working non stop as orchestrator of deepseek (the default setup of my skill) for something like 4 or 5 days (one plan to implement / session), So $20 + $5-10 of opencode go (that has the best deal on deepseek), you get a true workhorse, and in many cases, your tasks will be performed directly by deepseek in opencode without using any opus quota. But you will still have opus 5 access for elaborating plans, analysis etc that you can then either (if complex and long) use my skill, or just hand to deepseek in open code.   
AS far as usage goes, even among the chinese models, you won't get much better deals than what is included in the Claude or ChatGPT plans, even the $20 ones, so i highly suggest to keep one for some occasional heavy lifting.   
An additional tip to consider when trying to get the most bang for the buck, ChatGPT, $20 subscription, comes with basically unlimited use of Sol high via the chat interface. It is not as powerful or comfortable as using it via codex, but it gets you an unlimited back up (you can upload to the chat a full zipped project and it will work on it and give you a zip back) and a good analysis / plan maker. (plus, sol and luna together are a powerful combo, not as cheap as the opus / deepseek one but still a good option)

replies.author: Lavio00
replies.body: Oh, so you're saying I can stay in the claude app and use opus 5 as the orchestrator / planner there, and \*then\* separately in opencode go, deepseek will do the coding, activated by that deepseek-and-destroy skill? I didn't know one could use both the claude app and opencode go within the same session. They can talk to each other?

replies.author: orblabs
replies.body:
Yes !  😎   
My skill tells claude (or any other harness) how to talk with deepseek running on opencode basically. So you just have to install opencode (free) and subscribe to the $5 plan (first month), set the api key in opencode (you launch opencode, type /connect and it asks you to what, select opencode go, paste the api key and it is done).   
So you continue using only Claude app as interface, you talk with opus, and opus uses an army of deepseek cheap workers to get what it wants done.

replies.body: Just to be clear, deepseek flash is incredible especially for its price, but it is nowhere near opus (altho comparable to a very token wasteful sonnet 5). What i have been suggesting will be very cheap and very powerful, but it is a not a one to one replacement. Basically, "DISCLAIMER need to test a bit and see what works best for you" :)
